contents.name: SS12, Lemma 12.2: an injective O_X-module is flasque; Lemma 12.3: a flasque sheaf has vanishing Cech cohomology on every open covering
SS15, (15.0.1): the canonical comparison map from fixed-cover Cech cohomology to sheaf cohomology, natural in the sheaf and compatible with refinements
SS16, Lemma 16.1 (tag 09V1): H^1(X,F) from the refinement-limit Cech theory maps isomorphically to sheaf cohomology
SS16, Lemma 16.2 (tag 09V2): for Hausdorff quasi-compact X the Cech comparison is an isomorphism in every degree; boundary operators are built from local lifts and universality of delta functors
SS21 (tag 0A39): Gamma_Z(X,F) as the sections with support in the closed Z, with the support of a section defined in Modules Definition 5.1

sources.locator: SS10.2 pp. 178-179 (F_Z, Gamma_Z, equation (10.2.4)); SS11.1 pp. 201-207 (proper direct images, the support-proper description of f_!); SS11.2 c-soft sheaves pp. 207-210 (Definition 11.2.1, Propositions 11.2.2-11.2.13 with proofs); SS11.7 p. 221 (Proposition 11.7.2). Complete relevant sections read in the downloaded notes.

contents.name: Definition 11.2.1: F is c-soft if Gamma(X;F) -> Gamma(K;F) is surjective for every compact K
Proposition 11.2.2: equivalences between c-softness, surjectivity of Gamma_c(X;F) -> Gamma_c(Z;F|Z) for locally closed Z, and Gamma_c(X;F) -> Gamma(K;F)
Corollary 11.2.3 and Proposition 11.2.4: tensor product with a flat module and filtered colimits/direct sums of c-soft sheaves are c-soft
Proposition 11.2.5: c-softness is preserved by restriction to locally closed subsets, by f_! along any continuous map, and by extension F_Z of a locally closed subset
Proposition 11.2.6: for 0 -> F' -> F -> F'' -> 0 with F' c-soft, the compactly supported section sequence is short exact

Propositions 11.2.7 and 11.2.9 with Corollary 11.2.10: a quotient of c-soft sheaves in a short exact sequence with c-soft middle is c-soft, and F is c-soft iff R Gamma_c(U;F) is concentrated in degree 0 for every open U
Propositions 11.2.11-11.2.12: for X locally compact and countable at infinity, c-softness is injective with respect to Gamma and is a local property
contents.reason: These clauses assume the space is countable at infinity, which this pair does not assume and does not need; the proofs on this page are arranged so that no sigma-compactness hypothesis enters any statement.

contents.name: Proposition 11.2.13: over a field k, K tensor F is c-soft whenever F is c-soft
contents.reason: The pair only needs, and only states, the constant-vector-space case (a direct sum of copies of F); the general sheaf-tensor strengthening is not needed by the KLR consumers and would enlarge the page without a consumer.

contents.name: SS11.7 Proposition 11.7.2: for a C^0-manifold of constant dimension n, H^j(X;F) and H^j_c(X;F) vanish for j>n and the c-soft dimension equals n; proof resolves F by injectives and finishes with Proposition 11.2.9
SS10.2 equation (10.2.4): Gamma_Z(X;F) = {s in Gamma(U;F) : supp(s) contained in Z} for locally closed Z

sources.locator: SS1 pp. 338-340 (the functor f_! and its properties 1.1-1.4, including the c-mou terminology and the finite Y-soft resolution statement); SS4 p. 347 (cohomologically A-constructible spaces; opens of finite polyhedra); SS5 pp. 347-349 (submersive and constructible maps). Complete 14-page expose read in the numdam scan.

contents.name: SS1.1: f_! is the direct image with proper supports; it is left exact; for Y a point it is the compactly supported section functor; for open/closed immersions it is extension by zero / direct image
SS1.1 and SS1.2: sections with support proper over the base; base-change and the open/closed descriptions of f_!

SS1.4: f_! has finite cohomological dimension iff the compact-support cohomology dimension of the fibres is uniformly bounded; a sheaf is Y-mou iff it restricts to a c-mou (c-soft) sheaf on every fibre; Y-softness is equivalent to f_!-acyclicity of every open extension; if f_! has finite cohomological dimension every sheaf admits a finite resolution by Y-soft sheaves
SS1.3: f_! commutes with filtered inductive limits
contents.reason: Not claimed or needed on this pair: no filtered-colimit compatibility of compact-support functors is stated in the scaffold, and the property is left to the six-operations consumer that actually uses colimits.

contents.name: SS4 p. 347: any locally compact space locally isomorphic to an open subset of a finite polyhedron is cohomologically A-constructible
